summary: This short Informational document specifies an Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) identifier for CoAP services secured with DTLS. With an ID registered, both ends can agree during the handshake that they will speak CoAP.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9952 registers the ALPN identifier “co” for CoAP services secured with DTLS. It uses a short value to help limit handshake message size in constrained networks.

subtitle: Registers the ALPN identifier “co” for CoAP services secured by DTLS.

tldr.problem: CoAP services secured by DTLS need an ALPN identifier distinct from the one used for CoAP over TLS.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9952 registers the two-byte ALPN value 0x63 0x6f, the ASCII string “co”, for CoAP over DTLS.
tldr.outcome: The short identifier can reduce handshake message size in constrained networks. The document does not establish additional rules for using ALPN during a DTLS handshake.

today: RFC 9952 is an Informational document published in March 2026. It records IANA's registration of co for CoAP over DTLS.

sections.title: Identifying CoAP over DTLS
sections.content: ALPN lets communicating parties agree on an application-layer protocol during a TLS handshake. RFC 8323 already defines coap for CoAP over TLS. RFC 9952 registers a different identifier for CoAP over DTLS rather than reusing the TLS identifier.
sections.plainLanguage: ALPN names the application protocol used by a secure connection. This RFC adds a separate name for CoAP when it uses DTLS.

sections.title: The Short ALPN Value
sections.content: The identifier for CoAP over DTLS is co, encoded as 0x63 0x6f. The RFC says the short value can avoid fragmentation of ClientHello and ServerHello messages in constrained networks with link-layer fragmentation, such as 6LoWPAN. CoAP over TLS continues to use coap.
sections.plainLanguage: Use co to identify CoAP over DTLS and coap for CoAP over TLS. The shorter DTLS name can save space in constrained networks.

sections.title: Scope of the Registration
sections.content: Security considerations for ALPN and SVCB resource records also apply to this identifier. RFC 9952 says it does not change the behavior specified for CoAP by RFC 7252 and does not establish additional rules for using the ALPN extension during a DTLS handshake.
sections.plainLanguage: The registration does not add new handshake behavior. The security guidance for ALPN and SVCB records still applies.
